messages.body_plain:
First, thank you for making ggtree, it is incredibly helpful for my research.

I am able to plot my tree correctly, however I would like to label a clade of a tree (node 839 in this case). When I try to add a geom_cladelabel for the specified node, I get an error:

MRCA(mytree, tip=c('A51', 'A4'))

[1] 839
Warning: Ignoring unknown aesthetics: subset
Warning: Ignoring unknown aesthetics: subset
Warning: Ignoring unknown aesthetics: node, parent
Warning: Ignoring unknown aesthetics: node, parent
Error: stat_clad_bar requires the following missing aesthetics: xend, yend

I am using the most recent version of ggtree (). If you would like I can set up a test/example dataset/R script and upload that as well if you think it would be helpful.

Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: Plot mirror image of tree?
messages.subject_clean: Plot mirror image of tree?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jess,

reverse_x_scale() will do that. The tip labels will need to be offset a bit (hjust) since the default is to be left-justified to the end of the branch.

library(ape)
library(ggtree)
#makes test tree
tree <- rtree(5)
ggtree(tree) + scale_x_reverse() + geom_tiplab(hjust=1,align=FALSE)
ggtree(tree) + scale_x_reverse() + geom_tiplab(hjust=1,align=TRUE)

messages.subject: annotating trees with image files
messages.subject_clean: annotating trees with image files
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

With new version of ggimage (v=0.1.0), https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/ggimage/vignettes/ggimage.html, now geom_tiplab and geom_nodelab (both in devel branch) support more geom, e.g. geom="image", to label tips or internal nodes using image files.

See demo on https://guangchuangyu.github.io/ggtree-book/chapter-ggimage.html.

Besides, subview, phylopic and annotation_image will be removed in next release.
​

The overlap was introduced to solve conflict issue. For your last plot, there is no conflict exists and groupOTU do the right thing to traceback from t2 and t3 to their mrca.
In next release, I will introduce another parameter connect = FALSE (by default) to not trace back t2 and t3 to mrca in the situation we presented in your last plot that the induced graph contains only nodes with degree = 1. If setting connect = TRUE, it will always trace back to mrca.
